_readme: EHD Lab people. Edit this file on github.com to change the People page — no need to touch Squarespace. Photos live in docs/people/ and are referenced by filename only. Every field except 'name' is optional; anything blank is simply not rendered. Content transcribed from the previous ehdlab.ca/people page, August 2026.

_fields.name: Full name as displayed.
_fields.photo: Filename in docs/people/, or a full https:// URL. Blank shows initials in a coloured circle.
_fields.graduated: Alumni only. Card then reads '2019 – 2024' and the person appears under Alumni.
_fields.areas: PI only. Array of research areas, shown as a list in the right-hand rail of the PI card. Four to six reads best.
_fields.supervisors: Array of names. Shown inside the expanded Research panel.
_fields.note: Any extra line, e.g. a co-enrolment. Shown in the expanded panel.
_fields.now: Alumni only. Current position, e.g. 'Postdoctoral Fellow, TU Delft'.
_fields.orcid: Full https://orcid.org/... URL. Renders the ORCID iD mark.
_fields.website: Personal or group site. Renders a globe. An ORCID URL left here is detected and moved to the ORCID icon automatically.
_fields.email: Plain address; the mailto: prefix is added automatically.
_fields.research: The research summary revealed by the 'Research' button.

pi.name: Shooka Karimpour, Ph.D., P.Eng.
pi.title: Associate Professor of Civil Engineering, York University
pi.research: Dr. Shooka Karimpour is an Associate Professor of Civil Engineering at York University and Principal Investigator of the Environmental HydroDynamics (EHD) Lab. Her research focuses on turbulent mixing, multiphase flow, and microplastic transport in aquatic systems.

members.name: Behnam Nayebi
members.research: Behnam's research investigates the correlation between hydrodynamics and microplastic distribution in the southwestern region of Lake Ontario. His work explores how nearshore plumes, offshore currents, and thermal stratification influence microplastic patterns in water and sediment. He is developing new methods for sampling, preparation, and analysis to better understand how water movement and source proximity shape microplastic transport and deposition.

members.name: Siamak Seyfi
members.research: Siamak's research explores how turbulence influences the transport and settling of microplastics in aquatic systems through experimental studies using Particle Image Velocimetry (PIV) and Particle Tracking Velocimetry (PTV).

members.name: S.M. Hadi Mousavian
members.research: Hadi's research focuses on numerical modeling of fluid–soil–structure interaction, with particular emphasis on assessing the effects of hydrodynamic loads and local scouring on the structural performance of bridge piers.

members.name: Mohammadmehdi Ramezani
members.research: Mohammadmehdi's research focuses on turbulent multiphase flow using high-fidelity CFD approaches across a wide range of environmental and engineering applications. He investigates turbulent mass fluxes in hydraulic jumps and studies the settling of microplastics in quiescent and turbulent flows to improve understanding of their behavior under different ambient conditions and to enhance existing large-scale transport models.

members.name: Camillo De Castro
members.research: Camillo's research focuses on the experimental investigation of particle–particle interactions affecting the settling of microplastic particles in quiescent water. He analyzes the hydrodynamic processes involved in the mobility of microplastics in water to better understand their transport and fate in aquatic environments and to advance mitigation and prevention efforts against microplastic contamination.

members.name: Anastasiia Bolshakova
members.research: Anastasiia is doing a thesis on the weathering of microplastics during mesophilic anaerobic digestion of wastewater sludge.

members.name: Mohammad Ibraheem
members.research: Mohammad's research focuses on the detection and characterization of microplastics in permafrost thaw slumps. He completed his Bachelor of Engineering at York University, graduating in Summer 2024.

members.name: Vrashesh Karkar
members.note: Enrolled at the University of Windsor since January 2023.
members.research: Vrashesh's research evaluates hydrological models for simulating microplastic transport in the Credit River and Humber River watersheds, which drain into Lake Ontario. His work combines rainfall-event sampling and laboratory analysis to determine microplastic concentrations and promotes standardized methods for improving data consistency across studies.

members.name: Sejal Dave
members.research: I completed my undergraduate studies in Biology at York University and worked for a few years as a veterinary assistant before pursuing graduate studies. During the second year of my Master’s program, I transferred to the PhD program, where I am currently a PhD candidate under the supervision of Dr. Raymond Kwong and Dr. Shooka Karimpour. My research focuses on the effects of microplastics in the freshwater invertebrate Daphnia magna. I investigate how factors such as diet, water flow velocity, and different exposure durations influence MP biokinetics and physiological stress in Daphnia. My work integrates physiological measurements, including respirometry and oxidative stress responses, with RNA sequencing (gene expression) and proteomics (protein expression), to better understand the mechanisms underlying microplastic exposure in Daphnia.

alumni.name: Arefeh Shamskhany, Ph.D.
alumni.research: Arefeh's doctoral research focused on the transport of microplastics in aquatic environments, with particular emphasis on the effects of particle physical characteristics. Her work primarily employed computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to simulate the transport, entrainment, and vertical motion of microplastics in turbulent flow using high-resolution numerical models. She also conducted laboratory experiments to advance understanding of microplastic behaviour in natural water systems.
